column1: # Train the pi-flow on the FIVE VERTICES ONLY, then ask it for interior mixtures.
# A harder generalisation test than LOMO. LOMO removes ONE mixture and
# leaves 84, so the nearest surviving mixture sits at L1 0.17-0.40 and the claim is
# interpolation inside a dense simplex. This arm removes all 80 singletons and
# leaves the 5 one-hot anchors, so the nearest training mixture a target ever has
# is at L1 median 1.1315 (range 0.4385-1.4723) -- 4.7x the LOMO median. Learning to
# mix without having seen a mixture is a much stronger signal than leave-one-out.
# HOW THE ROW SELECTION WORKS, AND WHY IT NEEDS NO NEW FLAG
# train_flow.py keeps rows with l1(pi, center) > radius. L1-to-barycentre is
# MAXIMAL at the vertices, so a barycentre ball selects the anchors by complement:
#     every anchor            L1 = 1.6000 exactly
#     most extreme singleton  L1 = 1.1615  (then 1.1400, 1.1323)
# Any radius in (1.1615, 1.6000) keeps exactly the 20 anchor rows; 1.3 leaves
# 0.14 / 0.30 of margin on either side. Verified against
# reports/data/population/mini_b015/zoo_meta.json.
# THE BLINDING IS CORRECT, NOT A BUG. The ball is sealed into flow_meta.json and
# report_functional.score_generated uses it to shrink the retrieval pool to the
# same 20 anchors. The flow is forbidden the 80 singletons, so the lookup table is
# too -- that is exactly matched blinding. Expect "retrieval pool excludes 80
# member(s)" in the report.
# DO NOT run merge_gen.py on this arm: it hard-refuses radius > 1e-3 (default
# --max_radius), by design, so a blinded flow is never merged with an unblinded
# one. This is a single flow scored in a single job, so there is nothing to merge.
# nn_l1 below is the MEDIAN over the 80 interior targets, not a single target's
# value -- unlike a LOMO line, one arm here serves every target.
# tag
anchoronly
